design_condition: The long volume extends toward the plot boundaries, steps back on the north side, protects its eastern entrance, and forms a courtyard relationship with neighbouring buildings while leaving limited western open space.

positive.statement: The project creates a structured floor plan with a functional room arrangement.

position.rationale: Top view shows an elongated organized footprint with nested internal zones; elevations confirm a single low-level volume.

positive.statement: The straight corridors are advantageous in terms of safety and have optimal lighting.

position.rationale: Internal linear organization is suggested by the nested plan, but corridors are not individually distinguishable.

positive.statement: The easily accessible courtyard offers a large open space with maximum flexibility of use.

position.rationale: Central nested opening in the top view provides a clear courtyard-like open-space anchor.

positive.statement: The wooden ceiling elements and solid interior walls form a functional and economical support system.

position.target: wooden ceiling elements and solid interior walls
position.rationale: The sampled envelope supports a roof-and-wall system location, though material and interior construction are not visible.

positive.statement: The south orientation of the patient rooms offers attractive exposure and sunlight.

position.rationale: South-facing rooms are anchored along the southern building edge, with their interior subdivision unresolved.

positive.statement: The technical access, especially to the patient rooms from the corridor, is optimally solved.

position.rationale: A plausible corridor-side location follows the southern room band, but technical access is not separately visible.

positive.statement: The ecological construction approach responds to the limited period of use and gives the property a warm character.

position.rationale: Ecological performance and warm character are evaluative properties without a reliable geometric marker.

negative.statement: The extensive footprint makes the new building appear very autonomous in relation to the surrounding development structure.

position.rationale: Top and elevation views clearly show the long footprint extending broadly across the sampled model.

negative.statement: The pavilion expression does not correspond to the size of the object.

position.rationale: The low elongated mass and extensive footprint provide direct evidence for the overall pavilion-scale expression.

negative.statement: The entrance position is not entirely logical in view of the northern open space.

position.rationale: The eastern edge is the constrained entrance location, adjacent to the north-side open-space relationship.

negative.statement: The western outside space is limited and not spatially clearly defined.

position.rationale: The western perimeter is identifiable beside the long footprint, while the external landscape is not sampled distinctly.

negative.statement: The entrance area is somewhat tight.

position.rationale: The eastern building edge provides a plausible compact entrance-area anchor without a distinguishable entrance object.

negative.statement: The smoking area and internal facade are not clearly defined.

position.rationale: The central zone suggests an internal facade edge, but no smoking area is identifiable in the exterior sample.

negative.statement: The nearby facade severely limits the view from the patient rooms.

position.rationale: Patient rooms are constrained to the south-facing band; the obstructing nearby facade is not separately distinguishable.

negative.statement: The importance of the flat roof as a fifth facade should be taken into account.

position.rationale: The top footprint and highest elevation point rows provide direct evidence of a broad flat roof plane.
